key_insight: Patch-aligned features from foundation models (e.g., BLIP2) are highly redundant (≈90%); randomly selecting/stochastically dropping patches during training forces the policy to use non-redundant signals and improves out-of-distribution generalization for end-to-end driving.
problem_solved: Redundancy in self-attention-derived patch features harms robustness and OOD generalization of end-to-end autonomous driving policies; the paper addresses how to remove that redundancy to train more generalizable controllers.
method: Measure redundancy in foundation-model patch features using PCA and cross-patch similarity, showing ≈90% redundancy in BLIP2 descriptors.
Introduce stochastic patch selection during training: randomly sample a subset of patch features (drop redundant patches) so the policy learns to rely on diverse, robust cues.
Train end-to-end driving policies on the reduced patch set extracted from foundation models, improving OOD performance while reducing irrelevant feature dependence.
impact: Enables more robust, generalizable end-to-end driving policies that use foundation-model features more efficiently—reducing overfitting to spurious patch signals and potentially lowering compute and memory needs during training.
visual_elements: PCA scree plot showing that a small number of components explain most variance (annotated: ≈90% redundancy).
Cross-patch similarity heatmap to visualize redundancy across spatial patches.
Pipeline diagram: image → foundation-model patch features → stochastic patch selection (sample/drop) → policy network → improved OOD behavior.
Bar chart comparing baseline vs. stochastic-patch-selection OOD performance and a small icon/animation showing patches being removed.
paper_title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection
paper_authors: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus
